He [UNKNOWN] paused and then went on.

"And that leaves——just what exactly? Here's the position early on the morning of the 11th. Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong] has 'disappeared' (drowned). That leaves us [UNKNOWN] three people. I [UNKNOWN] killed Rogers [Thomas Rogers] on the morning of August 10th. He [Thomas Rogers] was chopping sticks for lighting the fire and did not hear me [UNKNOWN] approach. I [UNKNOWN] found the key to the dining-room door in his [Thomas Rogers] pocket. He [Thomas Rogers] had locked it the night before.

In the confusion attending the finding of Rogers [Thomas Rogers]' body I [UNKNOWN] slipped into Lombard [Philip Lombard]'s room and abstracted his [Philip Lombard] revolver. I [UNKNOWN] knew that he [Philip Lombard] would have one with him [Philip Lombard]——in fact, I [UNKNOWN] had instructed Morris [Isaac Morris] to suggest as much when he [Isaac Morris] interviewed him [Philip Lombard].

At breakfast I [UNKNOWN] slipped my [UNKNOWN] last dose of chloral into Miss Brent [Emily Brent]'s coffee when I [UNKNOWN] was refilling her [Emily Brent] cup. We left her [Emily Brent] in the dining-room. I [UNKNOWN] slipped in there a little while later——she [Emily Brent] was nearly unconscious and it was easy to inject a strong solution of cyanide into her [Emily Brent]. The bumblebee business was really rather childish——but somehow, you know, it pleased me [UNKNOWN]. I [UNKNOWN] liked adhering as closely as possible to my [UNKNOWN] nursery rhyme.

Immediately after this what I [UNKNOWN] had already foreseen happened——indeed I [UNKNOWN] believe I [UNKNOWN] suggested it myself [UNKNOWN]. We all submitted to a rigorous search. I [UNKNOWN] had safely hidden away the revolver, and had no more cyanide or chloral in my [UNKNOWN] possession.

It was then that I [UNKNOWN] intimated to Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong] that we [UNKNOWN] must carry our [UNKNOWN] plan into effect. It was simply this——I [UNKNOWN] must appear to be the next victim. That would perhaps rattle the murderer [Philip Lombard]——at any rate once I [UNKNOWN] was supposed to be dead I [UNKNOWN] could move about the house [UNKNOWN] and spy upon the unknown murderer [Philip Lombard].

Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong] was keen on the idea. We [UNKNOWN] carried it out that evening. A little plaster of red mud on the forehead——the red curtain and the wool and the stage was set. The lights of the candles were very flickering and uncertain and the only person who would examine me [UNKNOWN] closely was Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong].

It worked perfectly. Miss Claythorne [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] screamed the house [UNKNOWN] down when she [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] found the seaweed which I [UNKNOWN] had thoughtfully arranged in her [Emily Brent] room. They all rushed up, and I [UNKNOWN] took up my [UNKNOWN] pose of a murdered man.

I [UNKNOWN] had a rendezvous with Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong] outside the house [UNKNOWN] at a quarter to two. I [UNKNOWN] took him [Edward George Armstrong] up a little way behind the house [UNKNOWN] on the edge of the cliff [UNKNOWN]. I [UNKNOWN] said that here we [UNKNOWN] could see if any one else approached us [UNKNOWN], and we [UNKNOWN] should not be seen from the house [UNKNOWN] as the bedrooms faced the other way. He [Edward George Armstrong] was still quite unsuspicious——and yet he [Edward George Armstrong] ought to have been warned——. If he [Edward George Armstrong] had only remembered the words of the nursery rhyme, "A red herring swallowed one. ..." He [Edward George Armstrong] took the red herring all right.

It was quite easy. I [UNKNOWN] uttered an exclamation, leant over the cliff [UNKNOWN], told him [Edward George Armstrong] to look, wasn't that the mouth of a cave? He [Edward George Armstrong] leant right over. A quick vigorous push sent him [Edward George Armstrong] off his [Edward George Armstrong] balance and splash into the heaving sea below. I [UNKNOWN] returned to the house [UNKNOWN]. It must have been my [UNKNOWN] footfall that Blore heard. A few minutes after I [UNKNOWN] had returned to Armstrong's room [UNKNOWN] I [UNKNOWN] left it [UNKNOWN], this time making a certain amount of noise so that some one should hear me [UNKNOWN]. I [UNKNOWN] heard a door open as I [UNKNOWN] got to the bottom of the stairs. They [UNKNOWN] must have just glimpsed my [UNKNOWN] figure as I [UNKNOWN] went out of the front door.

It was a minute or two before they [UNKNOWN] followed me [UNKNOWN]. I [UNKNOWN] had gone straight round the house [UNKNOWN] and in at the dining-room window which I [UNKNOWN] had left open. I [UNKNOWN] shut the window and later I [UNKNOWN] broke the glass. Then I [UNKNOWN] went upstairs and laid myself [UNKNOWN] out again on my [UNKNOWN] bed.

I [UNKNOWN] calculated that they [UNKNOWN] would search the house [UNKNOWN] again, but I [UNKNOWN] did not think they [UNKNOWN] would look closely at any of the corpses, a mere twitch aside of the sheet to satisfy themselves [UNKNOWN] that it was not Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong] masquerading as a body. This is exactly what occurred.

I [UNKNOWN] forgot to say that I [UNKNOWN] returned the revolver to Lombard [Philip Lombard]'s room. It may be of interest to some one to know where it was hidden during the search. There was a big pile of tinned food in the larder. I [UNKNOWN] opened the bottom——most of the tins——biscuits I [UNKNOWN] think it contained, bedded in the revolver and replaced the strip of adhesive tape.

I [UNKNOWN] calculated, and rightly, that no one would think of working their way through a pile of apparently untouched foodstuffs, especially as all the top tins were soldered.

The red curtain I [UNKNOWN] had concealed by laying it flat on the seat of one of the drawing-room chairs under the chintz cover and the wool in the seat cushion, cutting a small hole.

And now came the moment that I [UNKNOWN] had anticipated——three people who were so frightened of each other [UNKNOWN] that anything might happen——and one of them had a revolver. I [UNKNOWN] watched them [UNKNOWN] from the windows of the house [UNKNOWN]. When Blore [William Henry Blore] came up alone I [UNKNOWN] had the big marble clock poised ready. Exit Blore [William Henry Blore]. ...

From my [UNKNOWN] window I [UNKNOWN] saw Vera Claythorne [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] shoot Lombard [Philip Lombard]. A daring and resourceful young woman [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne]. I [UNKNOWN] always thought she [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] was a match for him [Philip Lombard] and more. As soon as that had happened I [UNKNOWN] set the stage in her [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] bedroom.

It was an interesting psychological experiment. Would the consciousness of her [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] own guilt, the state of nervous tension consequent on having just shot a man, be sufficient, together with the hypnotic suggestion of the surroundings, to cause her [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] to take her [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] own life? I [UNKNOWN] thought it would. I [UNKNOWN] was right. Vera Claythorne [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] hanged herself [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] before my [UNKNOWN] eyes where I [UNKNOWN] stood in the shadow of the wardrobe.

And now for the last stage. I [UNKNOWN] came forward, picked up the chair and set it against the wall. I [UNKNOWN] looked for the revolver and found it at the top of the stairs where the girl [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] had dropped it. I [UNKNOWN] was careful to preserve her [Vera Elizabeth Claythorne] fingerprints on it.

And now?

I [UNKNOWN] shall finish writing this. I [UNKNOWN] shall enclose it and seal it in a bottle and I [UNKNOWN] shall throw the bottle into the sea [UNKNOWN].

Why? Yes, why?...

It was my [UNKNOWN] ambition to invent a murder mystery that no one could solve.

But no artist, I [UNKNOWN] now realize, can be satisfied with art alone. There is a natural craving for recognition which cannot be gain-said.

I [UNKNOWN] have, let me [UNKNOWN] confess it in all humility, a pitiful human wish that some one should know just how clever I [UNKNOWN] have been. ...

In all this, I [UNKNOWN] have assumed that the mystery of Indian Island [UNKNOWN] will remain unsolved. It may be, of course, that the police will be cleverer than I [UNKNOWN] think. There are, after all, three clues. One: the police [UNKNOWN] are perfectly aware that Edward Seton was guilty. They [UNKNOWN] know, therefore, that one of the ten people on the island [UNKNOWN] was not a murderer in any sense of the word, and it follows, paradoxically, that that person must logically be the murderer. The second clue lies in the seventh verse of the nursery rhyme. Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong]'s death is associated with a "red herring" which he [Edward George Armstrong] swallowed——or rather which resulted in swallowing him [Edward George Armstrong]! That is to say that at that stage of the affair some hocus-pocus is clearly indicated——and that Armstrong [Edward George Armstrong] was deceived by it and sent to his [Edward George Armstrong] death. That might start a promising line of inquiry. For at that period there are only four persons and of those four I [UNKNOWN] am clearly the only one likely to inspire him [Edward George Armstrong] with confidence. The third is symbolical. The manner of my [UNKNOWN] death marking me [UNKNOWN] on the forehead. The brand of Cain.

There is, I [UNKNOWN] think, little more to say.

After entrusting my [UNKNOWN] bottle and its message to the sea [UNKNOWN] I [UNKNOWN] shall go to my [UNKNOWN] room and lay myself [UNKNOWN] down on the bed. To my [UNKNOWN] eyeglasses is attached what seems a length of fine black cord——but it is elastic cord. I [UNKNOWN] shall lay the weight of the body on the glasses. The cord I [UNKNOWN] shall loop round the door-handle and attach it, not too solidly, to the revolver. What I [UNKNOWN] think will happen is this: My [UNKNOWN] hand, protected with a handkerchief, will press the trigger. My [UNKNOWN] hand will fall to my [UNKNOWN] side, the revolver, pulled by the elastic will recoil to the door, jarred by the door-handle it will detach itself from the elastic and fall. The elastic, released, will hang down innocently from the eyeglasses on which my body [UNKNOWN] is lying. A handkerchief lying on the floor will cause no comment whatever.

I [UNKNOWN] shall be found, laid neatly on my [UNKNOWN] bed, shot through the forehead in accordance with the record kept by my [UNKNOWN] fellow victims. Times of death cannot be stated with any accuracy by the time our bodies are examined.

When the sea [UNKNOWN] goes down, there will come from the mainland boats and men [UNKNOWN]. And they [UNKNOWN] will find ten dead bodies and an unsolved problem on Indian Island.
